Section: ## PARA 11.1
Part 3 of 3
==================================================
[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 10.7] (6) Where the compensator has failed to pay the agreed sum within 10 days, the claimant has the option to start proceedings using the procedure set out in paragraph 10.4 above.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 10.7] (7) After choosing any option apart from paragraphs (3)(a) or (b), the claimant may at any point start court proceedings.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 10.7] (8) A claimant who wishes to start court proceedings to recover any disputed fees in a claim to which this Protocol applies must use the procedure set out in Practice Direction 27B.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 10.7] (9) Paragraph 12.12 of this Protocol provides more information about the steps that a claimant must take if they wish to start proceedings to recover any disputed fees .

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 10.7] (10) The claimant should also consider seeking advice in these circumstances.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 10.7] Method of payment

## 10.8

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 10.8] (1) The method of payment is to be agreed between the claimant and the compensator .

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 10.8] (2) Where the claim for fees includes fees paid or payable by the claimant’s representative , the fees should be paid in any event to the representative .

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 10.8] The effect of settling the claim

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 10.8] 10.9 Settlement of the claim under paragraph 10.2 or 10.3 represents final settlement of all claims for damages for injury and for other protocol damages but does not prevent the claimant from pursuing any claim for non-protocol vehicle costs arising from the same accident outside this Protocol.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 10.8] Recoverable benefits and CRU

## 10.10

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 10.10] (1) In this Protocol—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 10.10] (a) “ CRU ” means the Compensation Recovery Unit, which is part of the Department for Work and Pensions and is responsible for recovering social security benefits in claims for personal injury;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 10.10] (b) “ Certificate of recoverable benefits ” means the certificate issued by the CRU to specify the benefits to be deducted from any damages and repaid under social security legislation; and

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 10.10] (c) “ deductible amount ” means any benefits or lump sum payment shown in the certificate of recoverable benefits , which the compensator is entitled to deduct in accordance with social security legislation.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 10.10] (2) The compensator is required by law to notify an injury claim to the CRU and to obtain a certificate of recoverable benefits before making a payment.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 10.10] (3) Certain benefits shown in the certificate of recoverable benefits must be deducted from certain types of payment for damages. Together, those benefits are known as the deductible amount .

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 10.10] (4) The certificate of recoverable benefits has to be valid at the time of payment and is valid only for a limited period, after which it needs to be renewed. The CRU is entitled to take up to 4 weeks from receiving a request to issue a certificate of recoverable benefits .

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 10.10] (5) The compensator should notify the claim to the CRU as soon as practicable after the claim is notified to the compensator .

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 10.10] (6) Where the compensator has obtained a certificate of recoverable benefits by the time an offer is made under paragraph 8.11, the offer must state the amount of any deductible amount , the name of the benefit and the item of damages from which it is deducted.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 10.10] (7) Where the compensator does not have a valid certificate of recoverable benefits at the time an offer is due, they must—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 10.10] (a) make an offer which is expressly subject to obtaining a valid certificate of recoverable benefits ; and

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 10.10] (b) not more than 5 days after receiving a valid certificate of recoverable benefits , disclose that to the claimant and explain whether any deductions are needed from the sum offered.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 10.10] (8) Paragraph (9) applies where, at the date settlement is agreed, the compensator does not have a certificate of recoverable benefits that will remain in force for at least 10 days.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 10.10] (9) The compensator should apply for a fresh certificate of recoverable benefits as soon as possible, notify the claimant that they have done so and must pay the amounts set out in paragraph 10.2 or 10.3 as appropriate within 30 days of the date of agreement.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 10.10] 10.11 The deductible amount may only be deducted from the appropriate items of other protocol damages and the compensator must tell the claimant —

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 10.10] (a) the gross amount of the offer, that is the amount of damages offered less any deduction for contributory fault but before any other deductions;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 10.10] (b) the amount in each case of benefits deducted from each item of damages;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 10.10] (c) whether (in the case of an offer for other protocol damages alone under paragraph 8.9(3) only) the deduction reduces the damages offered to nil.

## Claims for non-protocol vehicle costs

## Introduction

## 11.1

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 11.1] (1) Claims for non-protocol vehicle costs are handled outside the previous sections of this Protocol.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 11.1] (2) However, where the parties have been unable to settle the portal claim (see paragraph 11.2 below) under section 8 and the claimant wishes to start court proceedings to ask the court to assess the value of the portal claim , the court must be informed about all claims brought in the claimant’s name that are still in dispute. This includes any claim for non-protocol vehicle costs which has not been settled.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 11.1] (3) This section sets out the procedure that must be followed to ensure that the court has the information it needs about all parts of the claim , before proceedings are started.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 11.1] (4) The procedure must be completed before the claimant can generate the Court Pack under section 12 of this Protocol. Failure to provide information under this section may mean that any claim for non-protocol vehicle costs is not considered by the court and the claimant’s right to bring any such claim may be affected.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 11.1] Including the claim for non-protocol vehicle costs

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 11.1] 11.2 In this section, the term “ portal claim” means the claim for damages for injury and other protocol damages under this Protocol.

## 11.3

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 11.3] (1) Subject to paragraphs (2) and (3), where—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 11.3] (a) the parties have been unable to agree settlement of the portal claim ;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 11.3] (b) the claimant wishes to start court proceedings to assess the value of the portal claim ; and

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 11.3] (c) there is a claim for non-protocol vehicle costs being dealt with by another business or organisation separately from the portal claim ,

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 11.3] the claimant must first follow the procedure set out in this section.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 11.3] (2) Where the claimant is not the driver or owner of the vehicle in which they were injured, the claimant will have no claim for non-protocol vehicle costs and the rest of section 11 of this Protocol will not apply. The Portal will create the Court Valuation Form used in proceedings once the claimant selects the “go to court” button.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 11.3] (3) Nothing in this section prevents a claimant from starting court proceedings if they need to do so for limitation purposes.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 11.3] (4) Paragraph 6.7 of this Protocol provides that where the claimant starts proceedings to assess the value of their portal claim , any admission made in the Protocol is binding to the extent of all claims made in the proceedings. For the avoidance of doubt this will include any claim for non-protocol vehicle costs added under this section.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 11.3] (5) For the purposes of this paragraph, “owner” means the person by whom a vehicle is being kept and includes the person to whom a vehicle is leased or hired at the relevant time.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 11.3] 11.4 The steps required under this section must be taken before the Court Pack is prepared under section 12.

## 11.5

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 11.5] (1) The claimant must first set out on the Portal whether there is any claim for non-protocol vehicle costs .

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 11.5] (2) The questions on the Portal relating to non-protocol vehicle costs are intended to help the claimant to make the necessary enquiries, to obtain the information needed in paragraph (1).

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 11.5] (3) It is the claimant’s responsibility to obtain the information and to satisfy themselves that the information provided is accurate.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 11.5] (4) Support for unrepresented claimants who are unable to use the Portal can be obtained from the Portal Support Centre .

## 11.6

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 11.6] (1) Where—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 11.6] (a) the claim for non-protocol vehicle costs is added to the portal claim under paragraph 11.5 above; and

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 11.6] (b) following the step in (a), the claimant reasonably believes as a result that the overall value of the claim is more than £10,000,

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 11.6] the claimant may notify the compensator that this Protocol no longer applies to the claim .

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 11.6] (2) The Guide to Making a Claim provides further information on valuing the portal claim .

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 11.6] (3) The claimant should also consider obtaining advice in these circumstances.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 11.6] Non-protocol vehicle costs (“NVC”) claim document

## 11.7

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 11.7] (1) Unless paragraph 11.6 applies, the claimant must also complete the non-protocol vehicle costs claim document (referred to in this paragraph as “the NVC claim document”), which sets out the information and documents which the court and the compensator are likely to need in respect of the claim for non-protocol vehicle costs . The Portal will create the NVC claim document.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 11.7] (2) The NVC claim document must be supported by a statement of truth signed by the claimant .

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 11.7] (3) Where the claimant’s legal representative elects to sign the statement of truth , they must enter their name as confirmation that they hold the NVC claim document signed by the claimant .

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 11.7] (4) Where the statement of truth is completed by the Portal Support Centre on behalf of an unrepresented claimant , the Centre must tick the appropriate box as proof that they hold the NVC claim document signed by the claimant authorising them to do so.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 11.7] (5) Where the NVC claim document is completed by an authorised representative on behalf of the claimant , the statement of truth must be signed by the claimant in accordance with paragraph 1.3(3). The authorised representative must tick the appropriate boxes as confirmation that they have uploaded the NVC claim document including the statement of truth signed by the claimant

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 11.7] (6) The claimant must upload the documents required in support of the claim for non-protocol vehicle costs .

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 11.7] (7) The NVC claim document and the documents in support are sent to the compensator via the Portal .

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 11.7] (8) Support for unrepresented claimants who are unable to use the Portal can be obtained via the Portal Support Centre .

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 11.7] NVC response document

## 11.8

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 11.8] (1) Within 15 days of receipt of the NVC claim document, the compensator must complete the response document (known as “the NVC response document”) and upload onto the Portal any documents required in support. The Portal will create the NVC response document.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 11.8] (2) The NVC response document must be signed by the compensator with a statement of truth .

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 11.8] (3) The NVC response document enables the compensator to set out the information and documents which the court and the claimant are likely to need in respect of the Compensator’s Response to the claim for non-protocol vehicle costs .

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 11.8] (4) The NVC response document and any documents in support are sent to the claimant via the Portal .

## 11.9

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 11.9] (1) Once the compensator has complied with paragraph 11.8 or the 15 day period in paragraph 11.8 has expired, whichever happens first—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 11.9] (a) the Portal will create the Court Valuation Form used in proceedings;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 11.9] (b) the claimant may produce and send the relevant Court Pack list under section 12 of this Protocol.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 11.9] (2) Where the 15 day period has expired and the claimant has produced and sent the Court Pack list, the compensator may still send the NVC response document at any time before the relevant period for review of the Court Pack list set out in paragraph 12.6(1) has expired.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 11.9] (3) Failure to send the NVC response document as required by paragraph 11.8 or this paragraph may mean that the court will not consider the compensator’s arguments about the claim for non-protocol vehicle costs .

## Disputes – procedure to start court proceedings

## Introduction

## 12.1

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 12.1] (1) The Protocol permits the claimant to start court proceedings in certain circumstances.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 12.1] This will involve different types of proceedings for each of those circumstances. This section explains what is needed for each of those types of court proceedings.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 12.1] (2) Documents must be prepared for the court to use. These are put into what is known as the Court Pack. All those documents can be downloaded from the Portal and this section explains what is needed.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 12.1] (3) Paragraph 12.2 directs the claimant to the paragraphs in this section which deal with each type of proceedings. Each of these has a table which shows the documents to be included in the Court Pack for that type of proceedings.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 12.1] (4) Paragraphs 12.3 and 12.4 explain the steps the claimant needs to take with the Court Pack, before starting court proceedings.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 12.1] (5) The relevant court form must be prepared on the Portal , using information already captured from the claim to date and additional answers provided by the claimant . This is explained further in paragraph 12.7.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 12.1] (6) The Guide to Making a Claim gives more information about the steps that a claimant must take before starting court proceedings.

## 12.2

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 12.2] (1) The claimant may start proceedings under Practice Direction 27B, which is divided into section 1 covering general points and sections 2 to 11 setting out different procedures.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 12.2] (2) Depending on the type of proceedings required, the claimant should use one of sections 2 to 11 in Practice Direction 27B. Table 1 below explains where to find the procedure for each type of proceedings and how to follow the requirements of this Protocol.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 12.2] (3) The term non-protocol vehicle costs is abbreviated to “NVC” in the names given for the types of proceedings in the tables in this section and in the court forms.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 12.12] “ The Court Pack ” and notice of intention to start proceedings

## 12.3

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 12.3] (1) Before starting court proceedings, the claimant must prepare a Court Pack from documents held on the Portal as set out in Tables A to G, below.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 12.3] (2) When the claimant confirms their intention to start court proceedings, the Portal will automatically generate a notice to the compensator that the claimant intends to start proceedings, for the purposes of section 152 of the Road Traffic Act 1988.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 12.3] (2A) Where the claimant intends to start court proceedings to determine liability or due to limitation, the claimant must consider the overall valuation of their claim for court fee purposes and select one of the list of options on the Portal .

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 12.3] (2B) Where the claimant intends to start court proceedings to assess the value of the claim but has not made a counter offer showing their valuation of the claim , the claimant must complete the necessary details of their valuation on the Portal for court fee purposes including whether they say there is a whiplash injury .

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 12.3] (3) The Portal will determine the reason for starting proceedings from the steps taken in the claim . Where there are options provided for the reason, the claimant will first be asked to select the reason for starting court proceedings. This will enable the Portal to show the Court Pack contents from the relevant table.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 12.3] (4) The claimant selects the documents to be included in the Court Pack from those shown on the Portal . Once all the documents have been selected, the Portal will then generate a list (“the Court Pack list”) showing the documents selected.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 12.3] (5) The Court Pack list is generated on the Portal for sending to the compensator under paragraph 12.4.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 12.3] (6)Support for unrepresented claimants who are unable to prepare the Court Pack on the Portal can be obtained from the Portal Support Centre .

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 12.3] Sending the Court Pack list

## 12.4

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 12.4] (1) The claimant must send the Court Pack list to the compensator via the Portal—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 12.4] (a) no later than starting court proceedings due to limitation, but only where—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 12.4] (i) the claimant starts the process of preparing the Court Pack under paragraph 12.3 no earlier than 2 years 11 months after the date of the accident; and

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 12.4] (ii) no liability response has been provided by the compensator ; and

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 12.4] (b) in any other case (including where proceedings are started due to limitation after the compensator has provided their liability response) at least 5 working days before starting court proceedings.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 12.4] (2) The Portal will show the compensator which type of proceedings the claimant intends to start.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 12.4] (3) Where the claimant wishes to start proceedings for failure to pay an agreed interim payment or an agreed settlement within the time specified in this Protocol (the procedure in paragraph 12.12 and Table G (1) or G (2)), they must not do so if, before the end of the period specified in paragraph (1)(b) above, the compensator pays the agreed amount.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 12.4] Other linked claims

## 12.5

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 12.5] (1) Paragraph 5.8 explains the process by which the Portal runs a search for claims which are linked and automatically notifies the parties in each of these claims that there are linked claims.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 12.5] (2) Where liability remains in dispute at the Court Pack stage, the claimant will be asked when completing the steps needed under paragraph 12.4 above if they are aware of any claims by other persons arising out of the same accident . These may be claims being made under this Protocol or under other protocols or procedures.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 12.5] (3) This is so that the court form provides information to enable the court to consider whether directions are needed to link such claims together.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 12.5] Responding to the Court Pack list

## 12.6

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 12.6] (1) Save as provided in paragraph 12.4(1)(a) above, the compensator has 5 working days to review the contents of the Court Pack list on the Portal . The reason for the claimant starting proceedings will be shown when the compensator is reviewing the Court Pack list.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 12.6] (2) The compensator may add documents to the Court Pack list but may not remove any documents selected by the claimant . Where the compensator amends the contents of the Court Pack list, they must follow the procedure outlined in paragraph 12.9 to 12.12 below as applicable and send a corrected Court Pack list to the claimant .

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 12.6] (3) The claimant must then use the corrected Court Pack list to start court proceedings.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 12.6] (4) Where the compensator fails to respond within the period stated in paragraph (1), the Court Pack list is treated as agreed and the claimant may start proceedings.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 12.6] (5) Where the compensator intends to nominate a legal representative to accept service, the name and address and contact details of the legal representative should be provided to the claimant within the relevant period specified in paragraph (1) above. That address will then appear as the address for service in the court form.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 12.6] (6) Where there is no address for the defendant on the Portal and save where sub-paragraph (7) below or paragraph 12.8 applies, the compensator will be asked at this point whether they—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 12.6] (a) can provide an address for the defendant ; or

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 12.6] (b) wish to nominate a legal representative under paragraph (5) above, failing which the compensator will be named in the court proceedings as the defendant.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 12.6] (7) Sub-paragraph (6) does not apply in those cases where the claimant is permitted to use the procedure in paragraph 12.4(1)(a) above. In such cases the compensator will be named in the court proceedings as the defendant , unless there is an address for the defendant on the Portal .

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 12.6] Papers to be sent to court

## 12.7

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 12.7] (1) Where the compensator has either responded under Paragraph 12.6 or failed to respond within the period stated, the claimant will be prompted on the Portal to complete the steps needed to generate the papers to be sent to court.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 12.7] (2) The claimant will first be asked the necessary questions to complete the relevant court form as set out in Table 1 at paragraph 12.2 above.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 12.7] (3) The Portal will create the court form and the List of Documents for Court, which shows the documents to be included in the Court Pack and must be added to the front of the Court Pack when created.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 12.7] (4) The claimant must—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 12.7] (a) print off the court form and sign the statement of truth ;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 12.7] (b) print off the List of Documents for Court and the documents to be included in the Court Pack;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 12.7] (c) put together the Court Pack, with the List of Documents for Court at the front and the other documents in the same order as listed.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 12.7] (5) The signed court form and the Court Pack must be sent to the court with the relevant court fee to start proceedings.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 12.7] MIB or RTA Insurer as second defendant

## 12.8

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 12.8] (1) Subject to paragraph (2) below, where the MIB or an RTA insurer has responded to the claim under this Protocol as compensator and has consented to be named in the proceedings as a second defendant, this section will apply and the process under paragraph 12.7 above will create a court form showing the MIB or RTA insurer (whichever applies) as second defendant.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents (“The RTA Small Claims Protocol”) > 12.8] (2) Where no address for the defendant has been provided by either party by the time the claimant completes the step set out at paragraph 12.7(2) above, this Protocol will no longer apply to the claim.
